title: Northwind Commerce customer story (public) — outline v0
content:
WORKING DRAFT (v0) — Outline only. Do not forward externally.

Customer story goal
- Publish a developer-first case study for Northwind Commerce (ecommerce) that sells Dedicated + routing/fallback + cost controls.
- Primary use: late-stage enterprise deals evaluating Dedicated/Private; secondary use: inbound blog/Docs “Case Studies” landing page.
- Proof theme: “Predictable peak performance without runaway inference cost.”

Target reader persona
- VP Eng / Head of Platform / ML Eng Lead at an ecommerce or consumer marketplace.
- Motivations: p95 latency under load, predictable spend ($/1M tokens), resilience during peak traffic, ability to standardize serving without building an in-house stack.

Working title options (pick 1 later)
1) “Northwind Commerce keeps search + shopping assistant fast during peak events with Redwood Dedicated”
2) “From spiky latency to predictable p95: how Northwind runs AI search + chat on Redwood Dedicated”
3) “Dedicated capacity + smart fallbacks: Northwind’s playbook for reliable LLM shopping experiences”

One-sentence summary (for top of page)
- Northwind Commerce uses Redwood Dedicated and routing/fallback policies to power AI search and a shopping assistant with predictable p95 latency during peak traffic while keeping per-token costs under control.

Customer snapshot (public-safe)
- Company: Northwind Commerce (mid-market ecommerce)
- Use case(s):
  - AI-assisted product discovery (search augmentation + reranking)
  - On-site shopping assistant (chat for product Q&A, comparisons, order questions)
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Integrations (confirm what’s safe to name): CDN, app backend, vector DB, analytics/observability
- Peak seasonality: promotions / product drops / holidays (keep generic unless approved)

Problem statement (what was hard before)
- Customer-facing AI features are “always on,” but traffic spikes are not predictable.
- They needed:
  - Consistent p95 latency under load (site conversion is sensitive to delays)
  - No “surprise” throttling at peak
  - A safe failure mode when models/providers degrade
  - Cost controls that don’t require constant manual tuning

Constraints / requirements (make concrete; validate in interviews)
- Latency SLO: [TARGET] p95 for chat responses and search flows (separate if different)
- Reliability requirement: [TARGET] uptime or error rate target; “graceful degradation” acceptable (fallback model/region)
- Data considerations: avoid storing sensitive PII; keep request payloads minimal; logging controls
- Operational: small platform team; needed a runtime that “just works” without weeks of kernel tuning

Solution overview (what they built on Redwood)
- Dedicated capacity sized for steady-state + burst buffer (avoid overclaiming; confirm details with Markus/Simran).
- Routing policy:
  - Default model route for best quality
  - Fallback routes when latency or capacity thresholds hit
  - Optional regional fallback (if applicable)
- Cost controls:
  - Continuous batching + caching where safe (prefix/KV caching for repeated patterns)
  - Right-sized model selection per endpoint (search vs chat)
  - Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization profile suggestions) where used
- Observability:
  - Console dashboards for per-route token cost + latency breakdown
  - Error analysis + tracing hooks (only claim if used)

Architecture block (needs diagram; keep high level)
[INSERT ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM — owned by Simran Kaur; technical review by Markus Klein]
- Web/app → Northwind backend → Redwood Dedicated endpoint(s)
- Two primary paths:
  1) Search flow
     - Query → embeddings/rerank or retrieval augmentation (confirm exact steps)
     - LLM used for query rewrite / summary / ranking justification (if used)
  2) Shopping assistant flow
     - Chat → tool/function calls to catalog, order status, policies (confirm)
     - Response streaming enabled (confirm)
- Routing/fallback:
  - Policy triggers: latency threshold, error rate, capacity utilization
  - Fallback: compatible model variant or secondary route

Implementation details (developer-first; what engineers will care about)
- Timeline to first production endpoint: [X days/weeks] (confirm)
- Migration path: what they replaced (another inference provider? self-hosted?) — keep factual and non-comparative.
- Key technical choices:
  - Separate endpoints for search vs chat (or shared) — confirm
  - Token budgets / max context settings
  - Streaming settings (chat)
  - Safety / structured output (if used)
- Operations:
  - Rollout approach: canary/A-B or staged rollouts (only if true)
  - Monitoring: what they watch daily (p95, errors, $/req)
  - Incident handling: how fallback reduces customer impact

Results (metrics + outcomes)
NOTE: We likely need ranges, not exact numbers, unless Northwind approves exact values.
- Performance:
  - p95 latency before vs after: [PLACEHOLDER] (method + measurement window)
  - Throughput during peak: [PLACEHOLDER]
- Reliability:
  - Reduced timeouts / fewer incidents via fallback: [PLACEHOLDER]
- Cost:
  - $/1M tokens or cost per session change: [PLACEHOLDER]
  - Reduced overprovisioning due to predictable Dedicated capacity: [PLACEHOLDER]
- Business impact (if they will share, otherwise keep qualitative):
  - “Fewer abandoned sessions” / “higher engagement with assistant” / “more searches converted” (avoid hard conversion % unless approved)

Proof / measurement details (for internal use + Legal comfort)
- Define exactly how we compute:
  - p95 latency: from Redwood Console? from Northwind APM? which endpoint(s)?
  - Cost: Redwood usage analytics + internal allocation method
  - Time window: e.g., last 30 days excluding incidents (be transparent)
- Add a standard disclaimer line for published page:
  - “Metrics reflect Northwind’s workload and configuration during the measurement period; results may vary.”
- Flag: SUP-3812 (transient p95 spike) — ensure any published claim excludes that window or notes mitigations.

Customer quotes (placeholders; to be collected + approved)
- Quote 1 (VP Eng / Head of Platform): why Dedicated mattered (predictability, isolation)
  - [INSERT APPROVED QUOTE + NAME/TITLE]
- Quote 2 (ML lead / staff eng): why routing/fallback mattered (resilience under peak)
  - [INSERT APPROVED QUOTE + NAME/TITLE]
- Quote 3 (app dev): dev experience / time-to-value (API + observability)
  - [INSERT APPROVED QUOTE + NAME/TITLE]

Story angle options (pick the strongest after interview #1)
A) “Peak readiness” angle
- Dedicated capacity + routing policies ensure p95 latency holds during promo spikes.

B) “Resilience without quality cliff” angle
- Smart fallback keeps the assistant responsive; only degrade when necessary and in controlled ways.

C) “Cost discipline” angle
- Batching/caching + model selection + observability reduce per-interaction costs.

Narrative structure (draft)
1) TL;DR / hero section
   - 2–3 bullets: Dedicated, fallbacks, cost controls
   - 1 customer quote callout
2) Challenge
   - Peak traffic + user-facing latency sensitivity
   - Need for reliability and a safe failure mode
3) Solution
   - Dedicated sizing + endpoints
   - Routing/fallback policy design
   - Cost controls and observability
4) Implementation
   - Integration timeline
   - Key config/operational practices
5) Results
   - 3–5 proof points (metrics or ranges)
6) What’s next
   - Future expansions: more assistant surfaces, more languages/regions, evals/quality monitoring (only if they say)
7) CTA
   - “Talk to us about Dedicated / Private deployments” + link

Interview plan + notes placeholders
Interview #1 (Discovery + story)
- Attendees: Ethan (writer), Avery (AE), Markus/Simran (optional for tech), Northwind champion(s)
- Questions:
  - What user journey is most latency sensitive?
  - What broke first at peak previously: throughput, queueing, cost, errors?
  - What was their internal success criteria to greenlight Dedicated?
  - Describe the “fallback moment”: what triggers it and what happens?
  - What do they watch in production daily/weekly?
- Notes:
  - [PASTE NOTES HERE]

Interview #2 (Metrics + proof)
- Questions:
  - Can we share exact numbers or ranges?
  - Measurement sources and time windows
  - Any caveats we must include
- Notes:
  - [PASTE NOTES HERE]

Interview #3 (Quote capture + review)
- Questions:
  - Ask for quote candidates + titles
  - Review drafted quote options live (to reduce revision cycles)
- Notes:
  - [PASTE NOTES HERE]

Approvals + logistics (must follow reference program process)
- Verbal commitment: [DATE]
- Consent form: reference-program-consent-form-draft-v2 (Legal owner: Michael Grant) — final version TBD
- Northwind reviewers:
  - Marketing/Brand: [NAME]
  - Legal: [NAME]
  - Security/Compliance (if required): [NAME]
- Redwood internal approvals:
  - Product Marketing claims/proof: Soojin Lee
  - Technical validation/diagram: Markus Klein + Simran Kaur
  - CS readiness: Rachel Kim
- Review SLA requested: [X business days]

Risk / open questions
- What can we publicly name?
  - “Northwind Commerce” logo usage yes/no
  - Can we name Dedicated and routing/fallback explicitly?
  - Any restrictions on mentioning peak seasonality?
- Metrics constraints:
  - exact numbers vs ranges
  - whether cost numbers are allowed ($/1M tokens vs qualitative)
- Competitive sensitivities:
  - Avoid naming prior vendor unless Northwind requests it (and Legal signs off).

Distribution plan (draft)
- Primary: Docs site “Case Studies” + PDF 1-pager for AEs
- Secondary:
  - Blog post cross-linking to Docs page
  - Sales sequence insert for Dedicated/Private late stage
  - Optional webinar: “Peak-ready AI search + assistants” (partner angle TBD)

Next actions
- Avery: confirm champions + schedule Interview #1 (60 min)
- Markus/Simran: draft architecture diagram v0 + validate Dedicated sizing language
- Soojin: confirm messaging pillars + claim language allowed
- Ethan: after Interview #1, convert outline into a full draft (v1) + propose 2 quote options

Appendix: claim language guardrails (reminders)
- Avoid absolute claims (“guarantees,” “always,” “eliminated”).
- Use measured, attributable phrasing:
  - “Northwind observed…”
  - “During [time window], Northwind measured…”
- Keep fallbacks framed as resilience:
  - “Graceful degradation” / “automatic fallback policies” / “compatible model variants”
